newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electrics down, seen easing from June runup.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electrics down, seen easing from June runup.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures ended lower Thursday amidst some bearish fundamentals and as part of a gradual retrenchment from strong gains made in June, industry sources said.
"We saw a real runup over the past month with some generation units coming off, and now we're seeing a fairly slow decline from those levels," one futures broker said.
Lower natural gas prices, the return of some electricity generating units in the U.S. West and below-normal temperatures in the Pacific Northwest were also seen as bearish for electricity futures.
The lower prices were not seen as part of a large selloff, however. "We still have some good bidding support at these levels," the broker said.

August Palo Verde (PV) futures ended down $1.23 at $33.10 per megawatt hour (MWh) following exchanges in a range of $32.80-33.75, while September finished down 82 cents at $28.42 after trades in a range of $28.30-29.10 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds finished between 55 cents lower and 25 cents higher.

August California-Oregon Border (COB) futures closed off 29 cents at the day's high of $22.81 after exchange at $22.50-23.15, while September settled 24 cents lower at $22.71 following trades at $22.60-22.70 per MWh.
Remaining COB deferreds settled down between 10 and 35 cents.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 329 COB and 1,134 PV contracts traded.

Temperatures through the Pacific Northwest were forecast to be cooler-than-normal into early next week, while the Southwest was expected to see temperatures one to three degrees Fahrenheit above normal in the south and west and near normal elsewhere over the next several days.
In generation news, units expected to return to service shortly included the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Washington state and 1,080 MW San Onofre 3 nuclear unit in southern California.

The WNP-2 nuclear plant continued to await clearance from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission before beginning start-up operations, a spokesman for the plant said Thursday, adding the unit would be "physically ready" to resume operations by late tonight or early Friday.

Several Western coal-fired power units were also expected to return to the power grid beginning Thursday, including a 670 MW unit at Centralia, Wash., a 330 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and a 260 MW Hayden unit in Colorado.

Restart of the 300 MW unit 4 at the Reid Gardner coal-fired power plant near Las Vegas has been postponed to late Friday. The unit, which had been out of service since a boiler explosion on March 2, began to ramp up last week, but was curtailed this week for further testing and is now shut for a boiler chemistry problem.
August NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures finished down nine cents at $2.123 per million British thermal units.
